overall: Temperatures in NYC peaked unusually early at 77.0°F around 4-5am and have been declining steadily since, now sitting at 71.1°F at 10:52 ET with a sharp cooling velocity of -2.9°F/hr. This atypical morning-peak pattern, driven by mostly cloudy skies, onshore east winds, and an active shower/thunderstorm threat throughout the afternoon, is suppressing what would otherwise be a warmer day.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are broadly aligned in the 80-86°F range (ECMWF 81.1, NBM 80.8, GFS 83.9, HRRR 85.6), all well above the current running max of 77.0°F, which requires a meaningful ~10°F afternoon rebound from current levels. The intraday obs-driven model diverges sharply, placing peak probability in the 76-77°F bucket, reflecting the current cooling trend rather than a model-based afternoon recovery.
max_temp_prediction: The active Kalshi market uses odd buckets with the top bucket at 81-82°F (49.8% per D1_NOW), but the ensemble odd-bucket signal carries an abort flag and a reduce-50pct recommendation, reflecting the 3/3 hour disagreement from intraday observations. Afternoon warming is plausible if a break in clouds and storms allows even brief solar heating around the predicted 3:30 PM peak hour, but the combination of persistent east onshore flow, cloud cover, and storm interference makes reaching 81°F a stretch — a landing in the 79-81°F range is most likely, with 80-81°F as the central estimate and downside risk toward 77-79°F if storms fire earlier or clouds persist.
